title: Risotto al radicchio
subtitle: Venetian bitter chicory risotto
excerpt: A deep purple risotto from the Veneto, built on Treviso radicchio that melts into the rice and gives it a gentle bitterness balanced by Parmesan and butter. Visually striking, pleasingly unusual.
sourceNotes: Traditional preparation from the Veneto region of northern Italy, particularly associated with Treviso, where radicchio is a protected product. Cross-referenced with Giorgio Locatelli, Made in Italy (2006) for the classic Venetian risotto technique.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The soffritto can be made an hour ahead. Finish the risotto to order.

glossaryTerms.definition: The final step in Italian risotto-making where cold butter and Parmesan are beaten vigorously into the hot rice off the heat, creating a creamy, emulsified texture.

content.text: Risotto al radicchio is a winter dish from the Veneto. Carnaroli rice cooks in stock with radicchio di Treviso, which turns it deep wine-purple and adds a pleasant bitter note. A generous
of cold butter and Parmesan rounds the flavour at the end.

items.prepNote: hot, kept just below a simmer
cold, divided: 30 g for cooking, 50 g for mantecatura
finely grated, plus more to serve
radicchio di Treviso, about 250 g, shredded; substitute round radicchio if unavailable

content.text: Warm the olive oil and 30 g butter in a wide, heavy casserole over medium-low heat. Add the chopped onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and cook for 2 more minutes.
Add most of the shredded radicchio (reserve a small handful for garnish). Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until wilted and deep purple.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes over medium heat until the grains look slightly translucent at the edges. Pour in the wine and stir until fully absorbed, about 2 minutes.

Add a ladle of hot stock and stir constantly until absorbed. Continue adding stock a ladle at a time, stirring, until the rice is almost cooked (about 18 to 20 minutes). The rice should be slightly firm at the centre when you bite it; it will finish as you rest it.

Remove from heat. Add the cold butter in cubes and the Parmesan. Beat vigorously with a spoon until creamy and emulsified. Season with salt and pepper. Rest for 2 minutes with the lid on, then serve in warm bowls. Finish with the reserved raw radicchio and more Parmesan.

items.symptom: The risotto is stodgy and gluey
items.cause: Stirred too vigorously or too much stock was added at once
items.fix: Add stock in small amounts and keep the heat moderate. Stir regularly rather than continuously.

items.cause: The radicchio was not cooked long enough or the variety was very bitter
items.fix: Cook the radicchio for longer in the soffritto stage. A splash of red wine softens the bitterness.

items.symptom: The risotto is losing its purple colour
items.cause: Normal; heat affects the anthocyanins in radicchio
items.fix: Nothing to worry about. Garnish with the raw reserved radicchio to restore colour.

items.symptom: The rice is still chalky at the centre after 25 minutes
items.cause: Not enough stock was added or heat was too low
items.fix: Add more hot stock and increase heat slightly. Test frequently from the 18-minute mark.

content.text: Radicchio di Treviso has a protected designation of origin in the Veneto. The tight, elongated variety is more delicate than round radicchio and turns the rice a vivid purple as it cooks. The colour fades to a dull maroon in the heat, but the flavour deepens. It is a winter dish, when radicchio is at its best, and makes a striking first course before a simple main.
